title: Section 90 — Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage

content.overview: BNS s. 90 — Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage. BNS restatement of IPC 314. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 314. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 90 is the rule on “Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage”. The section provides that (1) Whoever, with intent to cause the miscarriage of a woman with child, does any act which causes the death of such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 90 exists so that “Death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
90. (1) Whoever, with intent to cause the miscarriage of a woman with child, does any act which causes the death of such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

(2) Where the act referred to in sub-section (1) is done without the consent of the woman, shall be punishable either with imprisonment for life, or with the punishment specified in said sub-section

Essential ingredients
1. (1) Whoever, with intent to cause the miscarriage of a woman with child, does any act which causes the death of such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
2. (2) Where the act referred to in sub-section
3. (1) is done without the consent of the woman, shall be punishable either with imprisonment for life, or with the punishment specified in said sub-section

Explanations
Explanation.—It is not essential to this offence that the offender should know that the act is likely to cause death

learningObjectives: Master the elements of causing death while doing an act with intent to cause miscarriage under BNS s. 90.
Contrast the sentencing frameworks: sub-section (1) act with consent (up to 10 years and fine) vs sub-section (2) act without consent (life imprisonment or up to 10 years).
Understand the statutory Explanation: knowledge that the act is likely to cause death is not required.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 90 penalizes doing any act with intent to cause miscarriage that results in the woman's death, punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years and fine under sub-section (1); and if the act was done without the consent of the woman, punishable with imprisonment for life, or with the punishment specified in sub-section (1) under sub-section (2).
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Imposes constructive homicide liability when an unlawful abortion attempt results in the fatal death of the pregnant woman, irrespective of whether the offender knew death was likely.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 90 (corresponding to IPC s. 314).
Sub-section (1): Act done with intent to cause miscarriage causing death of the woman — imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
Sub-section (2): Where the act referred to in sub-section (1) is done without the consent of the woman — imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to ten years, and fine.
Explanation: It is not essential to this offence that the offender should know that the act is likely to cause death.
essentialIngredients: The accused did an act with the intent to cause her miscarriage.
The act caused the death of the woman.
For sub-section (2): The act was done WITHOUT the consent of the woman.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 90 deals with fatal consequences arising from illegal abortion attempts. The provision establishes constructive liability: the offender's intent was to cause miscarriage, but the physical act resulted in the woman's death (for example, through toxic poisoning, perforation of internal organs, or septicemia). The statutory Explanation contains an important principle of criminal liability: the prosecution does not need to prove that the offender knew the act was likely to cause death. The unlawful intent to cause miscarriage is sufficient to transfer culpability for the resulting death. If the abortion attempt was undertaken with the woman's consent, sub-section (1) applies (up to ten years imprisonment); if done without her consent, sub-section (2) applies, exposing the offender to imprisonment for life.
examples: Teaching example (Unlicensed surgical abortion leading to death): An untrained practitioner attempts a surgical abortion on a consenting pregnant woman using unsterilized metal instruments. The uterine wall is punctured, causing fatal internal hemorrhaging. The practitioner is guilty under s. 90(1).

Teaching example (Forced abortion causing death): Assailants forcibly inject toxic chemicals into a woman against her will to terminate her pregnancy; she suffers immediate cardiac arrest and dies. The assailants are liable under s. 90(2) (life imprisonment tier).
distinctions: Section 90 vs Culpable Homicide (s. 100/103): In culpable homicide, the accused must intend death/grievous bodily injury likely to cause death, or have knowledge of likelihood of death; under s. 90, the intent is only to cause miscarriage, but death ensues.

Section 90(1) vs Section 90(2): Sub-section (1) applies where the woman consented to the miscarriage attempt (up to 10 years); sub-section (2) applies where the attempt was non-consensual (life imprisonment).
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who administered a dangerous dosage of abortifacient roots to a pregnant woman resulting in her death can plead absence of intention to kill as a defence.
Rule: Under the Explanation to BNS s. 90, knowledge that the act is likely to cause death is not essential to the offence.
Application: The accused acted with intent to cause miscarriage and that act directly caused her death.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 90.

keyTakeaways: Penalizes acts done with intent to cause miscarriage that cause the woman's death.
Sub-section (1): with consent (up to 10 years and fine).
Sub-section (2): without consent (imprisonment for life or up to 10 years and fine).
Explanation confirms offender need not know that the act was likely to cause death.
